name: Reflection Amplification
summary: Adversaries may attempt to cause a denial of service (DoS) by reflecting a high-volume of network traffic to a target. This type of Network DoS takes advantage of a third-party server intermediary that hosts and will respond to a given spoofed source IP address. This third-party server is commonly termed a reflector. An adversary accomplishes a reflection attack by sending packets to reflectors with the spoofed address of the victim. Similar to…

strategies.name: Detection Strategy for Reflection Amplification DoS (T1498.002)

analytics.name: Analytic 1140
analytics.guidance: Outbound spoofed traffic to known amplification protocols (e.g., DNS, NTP, Memcached) combined with abnormal network traffic volume targeting remote reflectors, resulting in disproportionate traffic returned to a victim

analytics.name: Analytic 1141
analytics.guidance: Spoofed outbound packets sent to amplification services from command-line tools or scripts, combined with abnormal outbound packet volume on known reflector ports

analytics.name: Analytic 1142
analytics.guidance: Command-line initiated UDP traffic bursts to external reflection amplification ports using built-in scripting or binaries with network anomalies

analytics.name: Analytic 1143
analytics.guidance: Cloud-hosted VM or container generates spoofed UDP requests to third-party services on known amplifier ports, with high outbound-to-inbound traffic ratios in VPC Flow Logs
